newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar heads lower on trade sales.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar heads lower on trade sales.

text.p: London's March white sugar contract hovered just above $300 support in solid turnover as a group of major players pressured the spot value in mostly outright sales, traders said on Monday.
March accounted for the bulk of the day's activity but managed to steer clear of the psychological barrier as bargain hunters bought the position at the lows.
Traders said some five major players, including trade and commission houses, were dominating the session. "The big boys are ruling the roost," said one.

"It seems to be trade-dominated as it nearly always is on the whites. There's a bit of switch activity going on," he said. Interest was noted in both the May/August and nearby March/May spread, which was trading in a range between 80 cents and $1.20. Sales of the March arbitrage widened the white/raw premium to $69, about a $1 wider than Friday's close.
At 1655 GMT March was $1.10 weaker at $301.20 after hitting an intraday low of $300.30. Market sources said $295.00 was likely to be the next downside target if $300 was broken.
May was down $1.30 at $299.80 and overall volume totalled 2,360 lots.
Paris nearby futures took slightly more of a pounding but volume stayed on the light side. March was down $2.50 at $300.50 and May down $2.00 at $300.20 in turnover of 243 lots.
